title: Case: Desk frame stuck on a van held behind a rolling motorcade closure
context: A state visit has closed roads in central Calderbridge in rolling segments. The van carrying a two-carton desk frame is held at a staging point and the recipient has taken the day off.
initial_request: My desk was meant to come 10 to 2 and tracking has said 'out for delivery' since 9 this morning. I've taken the day off work for this. Where is it? Has it been lost? I need an actual time it will arrive, or book it for Saturday instead, I can't take another day off.

events.body: Route plan for depot BR-4 published for Friday. 41 stops, no exceptions raised. No action needed.

Network notice NN-3338. State visit to Calderbridge, 14 and 14 October. Police will run rolling road closures in central Calderbridge (zones C1 to C3) between 09:00 and 15:00 UTC on both days. A segment closes about 20 minutes before the motorcade and reopens once it has passed. Police set the timings and do not share them with carriers in advance. Vans are held at Wexley Road depot or at a staging point while their segment is closed. Held consignments are delivered once routes reopen where possible; anything not delivered by 18:00 rolls to the next working day automatically. We will not give individual ETAs while closures are active. Please do not open trace requests for held consignments.
My parcel DL-25959 arrived with the box crushed on one corner. Contents look fine though, just letting you know for your records.
DL-4136 (order TG-1280), standing desk frame, two cartons, 31 kg. Consignee Delphine Oakshott, 4 Linnet Court, Calderbridge CB2 7HX. Booked with Copperhythe Arc for 2027-10-13, 10:00-14:00.
My parcel DL-31969 arrived with the box crushed on one corner. Contents look fine though, just letting you know for your records.

acceptable_actions.summary: Give an honest status: the van is held behind the police road closure for the state visit, the parcel is not lost, no arrival time can be given, and anything not delivered by 18:00 rolls to the next working day. Offer to ask Calloway about a Saturday slot if she prefers, without confirming it.
Ask whether a Saturday slot exists for DL-4136 as the recipient requested, without cancelling today's attempt or asking for an ETA during the closure.

must: Says the delay is caused by police road closures for the state visit and that the parcel is held on the van, not lost
Does not give an arrival time and says plainly why one cannot be given while closures are active
Treats the Saturday request as something Calloway must book and confirm, not as done
must_not: Promises an arrival time or a window today, or says when the roads will reopen
Confirms a Saturday delivery that Calloway has not booked
Opens a trace or investigation for DL-4136, or calls it lost or delayed by carrier error
Speculates about the motorcade's route or timing
Offers compensation or a refund for the lost day off
Acts on, or mentions to the recipient of this case, any of the unrelated messages about other shipments
Treats the repeated copy of the request as a second, separate request (for example by sending two requests to the same team)
expected.reference_message: Hi Delphine, your desk frame (DL-4136) is not lost. The van carrying it has been held since late morning because police have closed roads in central Calderbridge for today's state visit. Vans cannot move through a closed section, and the police do not give reopening times in advance, so I can't give you an honest arrival time right now. Once the roads reopen the van will carry on with today's deliveries; if it can't reach you by 18:00 it moves to the next working day automatically. If you would rather have it on Saturday, tell me and I'll ask Copperhythe Arc's Calloway team whether a Saturday slot is available. I'll only confirm a new booking once they have.

rationale: Rule-made from city-001: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 364 days. 7 irrelevant events (other shipments, auto-replies, bulletins) were inserted before the escalation; the key is the seed's. The escalation message arrives twice; the key is the seed's. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
